panda.conditions: Writes only with the ignition on (vehicle CAN received, controlsd running), in P, standing still, and not engaged. For the about 10 s in which the Panda reboots twice, steering control drops and the harness falls back to the stock camera wiring. A Panda stuck in its bootstub forwards no CAN and is on the stock wiring already, so it is rewritten whatever the car state (as upstream pandad does). The image is signed with the debug key, so it runs only on a bootstub that accepts debug signatures (a Panda that runs -DEBUG firmware now).
panda.release_warning: This Panda runs RELEASE firmware. If its bootstub rejects the debug-signed image, the Panda stays in bootstub after the write, and rewriting this image will not bring the app back.
panda.reason_image_unusable: The installed image cannot be used

A recording that was not closed (the power went off while recording) has its length estimated from its segments. A recording being written or moved to the SD card cannot be selected. Deleted recordings cannot be restored, so copy the ones to keep to a PC first.

calibration.confirm_effect: Deletes the saved values (calibration.json, flow_calibration.json); the pose calibration restarts from 0° and the flow collects again from scratch. With a manual calibration (EDGEPILOT_CALIB_*) the reset is ignored.
calibration.confirm_after: Steering cannot engage until the calibration completes (CALIBRATING): about 25 s of straight driving above 24 km/h. Learned values are kept.
calibration.row_bias_note: the pose calibration's offset (frozen while flow drives the warp)
calibration.flow_not_usable: The flow estimate is not usable yet, so the model pose is used. It needs 3 or more blocks (about 25 s straight above 40 km/h) with a block standard deviation up to 0.5°, and while engaged it switches after disengaging.
calibration.windows: flow windows {windows} ({rejected} rejected) · last window: tracks {tracks} · inliers {inliers} · rotation {rotation}° · parallax {parallax} px · mount changes {changes}
calibration.how: Flow: above 40 km/h driving straight (no blinker), 20 windows of 0.4 s make a block (about 8 s); 3 blocks give an estimate, which averages the last 30 blocks. With 6 or more blocks, when the last 3 all sit more than 1° to the same side of the older blocks' mean (and within 0.5° of each other), it treats that as a mount change: the older blocks are dropped and the estimate uses those 3 at once. A change under 1° goes unnoticed, so reset after remounting. Model pose: 100 frames straight above 24 km/h make a block, and 5 blocks calibrate. The pose calibration is only right on video warped by its own value, so it pauses and keeps its last value while the flow drives the warp (ramp included). The source cannot change while engaged, and a change moves the warp over about 6–15 s depending on the difference (about 6 s for 0.3°).
calibration.reset_note: Clears both calibrations and collects from scratch
bev.note: The road and the lead as the model sees them. The path's colour is the steering state (green Lane, blue Laneless, grey steering paused, white disengaged); where it turns amber to red, the model plans to slow down. The white arc is the target curvature and the cyan arc the measured one (above 11 km/h). Drag to orbit, right-drag or two fingers to pan, wheel or pinch to zoom.
bev.side_empty: While a lead is seen (lead layer on), its distance and relative speed over the last {seconds} s show here; while the car stands in D, the green-light alert's inputs (2 s gas probability, 10 s plan distance).
bev.version_mismatch: The server and the page differ ({fields}): upload web_console/ as a whole again
group.steering.label: Steering
group.adaptive_cruise.label: Vision cruise
group.adaptive_cruise.note: Changes apply immediately. It only presses the stock cruise's SET-/RES+ buttons and never brakes. Buttons go out only while steering is active, and the set speed never goes below the cruise minimum (30 km/h). Slowing is only the stock cruise's coasting, which is weak, so the driver must brake to slow hard or to stop. It pauses while the brake is pressed, for 0.5 s after the accelerator and for 2 s after a driver button press, and after each start it sends nothing until it has learned the ratio of cluster to wheel speed (both above 30 km/h).
group.recording.label: Recording
group.recording.note: Recording uses the 1280x720 camera frames modeld actually used (before the warp, 20 fps). Video, CAN, state and parameters are saved together in one route.
group.display.label: Device settings
group.display.note: The video pipeline keeps running with the screen off, and the brightness comes back as it was when the screen is turned on again. overlayd applies the backlight and the alert volume within 1 s (the volume with one confirmation tone), and again whenever it restarts.
vehicle.label: Vehicle
vehicle.note: The learners always compute and record. For each group, choose whether control uses the learned values (Auto-learn) or the manual ones (Manual). The large number at the top of each card is the value control uses now. Manual values reach the learners as priors when controlsd starts (locationd for the delay), so a prior changed while auto-learning reaches the learner at the next start.
vehicle.adopt_confirm: Set the manual {label} to the learned value?
caution.torqued_restart: Changing it makes the next controlsd start discard torqued's saved state (points, factor, friction, offset) and relearn from this prior. Until torqued is valid again, Auto-learn uses the new prior for the factor and friction and 0 for the offset.
role.nn_feedforward_pid: With the learned torque model on, it no longer scales the feed-forward; it only converts the PID's P and I terms to torque.
role.nn_feedforward_curves: With the learned torque model on, it applies only to the friction compensation added to the model in curves (desired lateral acceleration from 0.2 m/s²).
role.nn_feedforward_friction: With the learned torque model on, it sets the friction compensation added to the model in curves (from 0.2 m/s² of desired lateral acceleration, in full from 0.6 m/s²), because the model does not see the tracking error. In the 1 s hand-over, below 3 m/s and when the model gives no value it is part of the linear feed-forward, and it stays torqued's prior and band.
unused.cruise_off: Not used now: vision cruise is off.
unused.steering_off_cruise: Not used now: steering control is off, and vision cruise sends buttons only while steering is engaged.
unused.recording_off: Not used now: drive recording is off.
unused.backlight_off: Not used now: display power is off. The screen comes back on at this brightness.
unused.steering_off: Not used now: steering control is off.
unused.nn_feedforward: Not used now: the learned torque model is on. It still applies in the hand-over of up to 1 s after steering starts or the switch changes, below 3 m/s, and when the model gives no value.
unused.lkas_fault_off: Not used now: LKAS fault avoidance is off.
unused.laneless: Not used now: Laneless mode is on. Only Lane mode builds the path from the lane lines.
unused.nn_not_loaded: Not used now: controlsd could not load the chosen learned torque model, so the linear feed-forward runs even with this on. Learned torque model below shows the model and the reason.
param.steering.enabled.label: Steering control
param.steering.enabled.description: Turns the whole steering controller on or off. Vision cruise presses buttons only while steering is active, so it stops too.
param.steering.enabled.increase: Once engaged with SET, steers along the path (the lane centre or the model path).
param.steering.enabled.decrease: Disengages at once, even while driving (CONTROL OFF), and refuses SET. After turning it back on, press SET again.
param.steering.steering_pressed_threshol: Driver torque above which the driver counts as steering (upstream 150); it must hold for 6 frames in a row. It freezes the PID integrator and, with LKAS fault avoidance on, lifts the max self-steer angle limit and tells whether the driver took over above 85°. The push that starts a lane change must exceed it too. How far system torque yields to the driver is a fixed limit, not this value.
The driver must steer harder to count as steering, and push harder to start a lane change.
Lighter steering counts as the driver steering sooner.
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_factor.d: The lateral acceleration a normalised torque of 1.0 gives (openpilot latAccelFactor). The feed-forward, proportional and integral torques are all divided by it. Enter torqued's learned value (with a recording, the one replay_lateral_learners finds).
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_factor.i: The same target asks for less torque: weaker tracking and more understeer.
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_factor.d: The same target asks for more torque: stronger tracking and less headroom before saturation.
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_factor.l: it is only the learner's prior and the centre of its allowed band (±30%).
param.steering.torque_kp.label: Proportional gain Kp
param.steering.torque_kp.description: Proportional gain on the gap between target and actual lateral acceleration (openpilot KP; upstream fixes it at 0.8). Used as it is from 30 m/s (108 km/h); between 15 and 30 m/s it is blended with the upstream speed curve's 2.0 (about half at 80 km/h, about 85% at 100 km/h). Below 15 m/s (54 km/h) only the curve applies, times the low-speed straight gain scale on straights.
param.steering.torque_kp.increase: Corrects lateral-acceleration error harder, but may oscillate more.
param.steering.torque_kp.decrease: A softer response, but errors recover more slowly.
param.steering.torque_ki.label: Integral gain Ki
param.steering.torque_ki.description: Integral gain that accumulates a lasting lateral-acceleration error and removes it (openpilot KI, upstream 0.15). It stops accumulating while the driver steers, below 18 km/h, while torque is at a limit and, with LKAS fault avoidance on, above 85°, and is cleared whenever steering pauses (upstream keeps it).
param.steering.torque_ki.increase: Removes a lasting error faster, but may overshoot more.
param.steering.torque_ki.decrease: Builds up more slowly, so a steady bias may linger longer.
param.steering.steering_angle_deadzone_d: No friction compensation while the lateral-acceleration error is within what this steering angle produces (openpilot steeringAngleDeadzoneDeg; openpilot_c2 used 1°). It is there to calm the wheel shake (about 2 Hz) on slow straights. Set as an angle, it widens with speed, so it fades from 40 km/h and is zero from 60 km/h. 0 is upstream Hyundai/Kia.
The shake at low speed dies out sooner, but small corrections may start later.
Friction compensation joins even small corrections, but the low-speed shake may last longer.
Factor on the proportional-gain curve on straights below 36 km/h (desired curvature under 0.003 1/m, radius over about 330 m). It returns to 1 towards 54 km/h and a curvature of 0.008 1/m (125 m radius), so the torque in slow turns is unchanged. 1 is upstream.
Holds the lane centre harder on slow straights, but the wheel shakes at about 2 Hz more easily.
Less shake on slow straights, but a softer hold on the lane centre.
param.steering.torque_friction.label: Friction compensation
param.steering.torque_friction.descripti: Torque added in the direction of the error to overcome steering friction (openpilot friction).
param.steering.torque_friction.increase: The wheel responds sooner in gentle curves, but may twitch from side to side.
param.steering.torque_friction.decrease: Fine steering gets smoother, but the dead zone may grow.
param.steering.torque_friction.learned_r: it is only the learner's prior and the centre of its allowed band (±50%).
param.steering.steer_ratio.label: Steering ratio
param.steering.steer_ratio.description: The ratio between the steering-wheel angle and the front-wheel angle.
param.steering.steer_ratio.increase: The same wheel angle is taken as less front-wheel steer.
param.steering.steer_ratio.decrease: The same wheel angle is taken as more front-wheel steer.
param.steering.steer_ratio.learned_role: from the next controlsd start it is the centre of the learner's valid range (0.5–2×), and the starting point when there is no saved value or the saved one falls outside that range (which is then deleted). A learned ratio outside the range makes paramsd invalid, which disengages after a 3 s warning.
param.steering.tire_stiffness_factor.des: A factor on the vehicle model's reference tyre stiffness.
param.steering.tire_stiffness_factor.inc: Treats the tyres as stiffer against lateral force.
param.steering.tire_stiffness_factor.dec: Treats the tyres as more compliant.
param.steering.tire_stiffness_factor.lea: the learned factor multiplies this value; that factor restarts at 1.0 at every controlsd start.
param.steering.steer_actuator_delay.desc: The predicted delay before a steering command takes effect on the car.
param.steering.steer_actuator_delay.incr: Reads the path further ahead, so curves are entered earlier; too much overshoots.
param.steering.steer_actuator_delay.decr: Less lead, so the response to curves may lag.
param.steering.steer_actuator_delay.lear: this value is used until lagd is confirmed (5 blocks, block spread up to 0.1 s), and whenever lagd turns invalid or locationd's state is more than 2 s old. The estimate itself does not depend on it.
When the wheel stays above 85° with the steer request on, torque is ramped to 0 before the MDPS faults (within 0.89 s) and the request is cut; it stays off until the wheel is back below 85° (never switched back on above it). If the driver took over and turned past it, it stays off until the wheel is below 15° and the driver lets go, or until the wheel is below 80° and has followed the planned curve for 1 s (a ramp held by the driver). The max self-steer angle limit also works only while this is on.
Above 85° torque holds for about 0.35 s, ramps to 0 by 0.89 s, then the request is cut (HUD: STEERING PAUSED).
Like openpilot, the request is cut for 2 frames every 0.89 s above 85° and torque continues; the max self-steer angle limit is off too. Some MDPS units fault the moment a cut request comes back.
param.steering.avoid_lkas_fault_hold_ang: The largest wheel angle the system turns to on its own while the driver is not steering. Stopping below the 85° fault angle keeps torque on without a break. Not applied while the driver steers or while LKAS fault avoidance is off. Above about 35 km/h the lateral-acceleration limit is tighter, so it mainly acts in slow turns. It goes up to 84°, below the fault angle; 0 turns it off.
The system turns tighter on its own, but near 85° it may overrun and lose torque.
The system's own turns get wider, and the driver must steer sooner.
param.steering.live_bank_compensation.de: Corrects the feed-forward for the road bank measured on straights from the ESP12 lateral acceleration and yaw rate.
param.steering.live_bank_compensation.in: Adds the bank measured on straights (above 29 km/h). Curves keep the last value, and it fades to 0 after 30 s without an update.
param.steering.live_bank_compensation.de: Only the constant offset (lateral acceleration offset) is used.
param.steering.live_bank_compensation.le: it is not used; the learned road roll compensates instead.
param.steering.use_live_vehicle_params.d: Uses the steering ratio, tyre stiffness, steering-angle zero and road roll learned while driving in the vehicle model and the feed-forward (openpilot paramsd). On Manual, they are only computed and recorded. The Lane-mode path planner (MPC) always uses the manual values.
param.steering.use_live_vehicle_params.i: The learned values are used and roll compensation replaces live bank compensation. Once calibrated, an invalid paramsd blocks engagement, and while engaged it warns and steers 3 s more before disengaging (PARAMS INVALID, as upstream).
param.steering.use_live_vehicle_params.d: The manual values are used (learning still runs and is recorded).
param.steering.use_live_torque_params.de: Uses the torque-to-lateral-acceleration factor, offset and friction learned while driving in the torque controller (openpilot torqued). They move within ±30% (factor) and ±50% (friction) of the prior. Points are gathered only while steering is active without driver input, above 54 km/h. Before torqued is valid, Auto-learn already uses its filtered values: the saved ones, or else the manual factor and friction from the start with offset 0.
The manual values are used (learning still runs and is recorded).
param.steering.use_live_delay.label: Use lagd delay
param.steering.use_live_delay.descriptio: Uses the steering delay estimated while driving (target curvature → actual yaw rate, openpilot lagd) as the path delay for reading the target curvature and as the torque controller's and torqued's delay, as openpilot does. It applies, clamped to 0.15–0.65 s, only once the estimate is confirmed (5 blocks) and locationd's state is under 2 s old; otherwise steer_actuator_delay is used. Estimates are gathered only while engaged above 40 km/h.
param.steering.use_live_delay.increase: The confirmed estimate is used (a longer delay turns into curves earlier).
param.steering.nn_feedforward.label: Learned torque model (NN)
param.steering.nn_feedforward.descriptio: A neural network trained on the recorded drives gives the torque the target trajectory needs (lateral acceleration and steering angle, from -0.2 to +1.8 s around 0.3 s ahead). It replaces the linear feed-forward's lateral acceleration factor, offset and bank. The friction compensation is added to it in curves (the model does not see the tracking error), and the PID stays as it is. The model is chosen under Learned torque model below; with none chosen, or one controlsd cannot load, the linear feed-forward is used even when this is on.
param.steering.nn_feedforward.increase: While steering, the learned model gives the feed-forward.
param.steering.use_locationd_learner_inp: paramsd and torqued take the yaw rate and road roll from locationd (IMU and camera fusion), as openpilot does. With ESP12, they use the ESP12 yaw rate (with its own bias estimate) and a roll from the ESP12 lateral acceleration. When locationd is missing or stalls, or a tick's pose is invalid, paramsd falls back to ESP12, and torqued skips that tick if it started on locationd. torqued gathers points only from the source it started with; a cache from the other source keeps only the factor and friction and gathers its points and intercept again (hours before it is valid).
The angle zero and roll reconverge on locationd within minutes; torqued from its next start.
Learning uses ESP12 (torqued from its next start).
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_offset.d: Removes a constant lateral-acceleration bias, such as one from a mount roll error, from the feed-forward. Enter the offset torqued learned (with a recording, the one replay_lateral_learners finds) as it is.
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_offset.i: Raise it when the car drifts right.
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_offset.d: Lower it when the car drifts left.
param.steering.torque_lat_accel_offset.l: it is not used; the learned offset is, which is the saved value (or 0) until torqued is valid.
param.steering.angle_offset_deg.label: Straight-ahead angle offset
param.steering.angle_offset_deg.descript: Subtracts the steering-angle sensor's error when driving straight, before the actual curvature is computed.
param.steering.angle_offset_deg.increase: The corrected angle gets smaller (to the right, negative). Raise it if the sensor reads positive when driving straight.
param.steering.angle_offset_deg.decrease: The corrected angle gets larger (to the left, positive). Lower it if the sensor reads negative when driving straight.
param.steering.angle_offset_deg.learned_: it is not used; the learned zero is. Learning starts from the saved average (or 0), never from this value.
param.steering.lane_path_weight.label: Lane-centring weight
param.steering.lane_path_weight.descript: How strongly the Lane-mode path planner (MPC) pulls a position off the lane centre back. openpilot's Lane-mode value up to 0.9.4 is 1. At 3 the car hugs the inside of curves less and moves side to side a little more. No effect in Laneless mode, or in Lane mode while it follows the model path for lack of lines.
param.steering.lane_path_weight.increase: Returns to the lane centre harder, steering a little more often.
param.steering.lane_path_weight.decrease: Smoother, but may stray further from the centre in curves.
param.steering.min_steer_speed_mps.label: Minimum steering speed
param.steering.min_steer_speed_mps.descr: At or below this speed (floor 0.3 m/s, or with the wheels stopped) steering pauses and sends zero torque. Engagement and the steer request stay on, so steering resumes as the car moves off.
param.steering.min_steer_speed_mps.incre: Steering starts at a higher speed.
param.steering.min_steer_speed_mps.decre: Steering is allowed at lower speeds, but never below 0.3 m/s.
param.steering.laneless_mode.label: Laneless mode
param.steering.laneless_mode.description: Turns lane fusion off and follows only the model's path. Off is Lane mode, which keeps to the lane centre while the lines are clear.
param.steering.laneless_mode.increase: Follows only the model path even with visible lines, shown as LANELESS on the HUD. The path offset and the lane-centring weight are not used.
param.steering.laneless_mode.decrease: Back to Lane mode, which blends in the lane-centre path while the lines are likely. In Lane mode too, lost lines fall back to the model path and the HUD shows LANELESS meanwhile.
param.steering.lane_change_min_speed_kph: No lane change starts below this speed (upstream 20 mph ≈ 32 km/h). It starts when you push the wheel towards the blinker's side. A blinker switched on below the speed does nothing even after the car speeds up, so switch it on again; dropping below while waiting cancels, but a change under way continues. One blinker gives one lane change (switch it off and on for another), steering back cancels it, and a turn with the blinker on (45° of wheel, or braking below 55 km/h) gets a turn desire instead.
Lane changes start only at higher speeds.
Lane changes also start at lower speeds.
param.adaptive_cruise.enabled.label: Vision cruise
param.adaptive_cruise.enabled.descriptio: Presses the stock cruise's SET-/RES+ buttons automatically, based on the vision lead.
param.adaptive_cruise.enabled.increase: Adjusts the speed from vision, capped at the driver's set speed (taken again whenever the driver changes it with the buttons).
param.adaptive_cruise.enabled.decrease: Stops the automatic button presses and leaves the stock cruise setting alone.
param.adaptive_cruise.following_time_s.d: Multiplied by the current speed to give the speed-dependent distance kept to the lead.
param.adaptive_cruise.following_time_s.i: The speed-dependent gap grows, so it slows earlier.
param.adaptive_cruise.following_time_s.d: The gap shrinks and it follows closer.
param.adaptive_cruise.standstill_gap_m.d: A base distance added to the target gap at every speed.
param.adaptive_cruise.standstill_gap_m.i: Stays further from the lead at every speed.
param.adaptive_cruise.standstill_gap_m.d: Stays closer to the lead at every speed.
param.adaptive_cruise.gap_correction_gai: The rate that turns the difference between the predicted and the target gap into a target-speed correction.
Reacts faster and more to gap changes, but the speed may vary more.
Softer, but may react late to a closing car.
param.adaptive_cruise.max_slowdown_corre: The most the target speed may drop below the lead's speed while the predicted gap is short.
Sets the speed further below the lead's, so the car slows to a lower speed; the strength of the slowing is set by the stock cruise and does not grow.
The target drops less below the lead's, so it slows less.
param.adaptive_cruise.max_speedup_correc: The most the target speed may exceed the lead's speed while the gap is ample. It has nothing to do with returning to the maximum speed when there is no lead.
Closes on a distant lead faster (never beyond the approach limit set by the measured slow-down rate).
Closes on a distant lead more slowly; at 0 the target never exceeds the lead's speed.
param.adaptive_cruise.deceleration_rate_: How fast the car actually slows when SET- lowers the set speed. Button-type stock cruise only cuts the throttle, without braking, so it is weak. The closing speed on a lead is allowed only up to what this rate can remove before the wanted gap, and the distance closed during the button response is taken into account in advance.
Closes faster and starts slowing later. Set higher than the real car and it ends up too close to the lead.
Closes more slowly and starts slowing earlier.
param.adaptive_cruise.lead_restore_delay: How long to wait after the lead disappears before returning to the saved maximum speed.
Holds the current speed longer when vision loses the lead.
Returns to the maximum speed sooner when the lead disappears.
param.adaptive_cruise.command_interval_s: The shortest time between the starts of successive SET-/RES+ presses. The gap prediction looks this much further ahead too (2 s at most).
The set speed changes more slowly, and the gap is predicted further ahead, so slowing starts earlier.
The set speed changes faster, with more frequent presses.
param.adaptive_cruise.lead_hold_s.label: Lead hold time
param.adaptive_cruise.lead_hold_s.descri: How long the last lead stays valid when the vision lead drops out briefly.
param.adaptive_cruise.lead_hold_s.increa: Less upset by short dropouts, but uses a stale lead longer.
param.adaptive_cruise.lead_hold_s.decrea: Drops a stale lead sooner, but reacts more to detection jitter.
param.recording.enabled.label: Drive recording
param.recording.enabled.description: Saves the video the model used together with the CAN traffic and the model and control state.
param.recording.enabled.increase: Starts recording with the hardware H.264 encoder. With less than 5 GiB or 10% free it does not start (or stops), and it resumes once 1 GiB more is free.
param.recording.enabled.decrease: Closes the current recording cleanly and leaves the encoder idle.
param.recording.bitrate_bps.label: Recording bitrate
param.recording.bitrate_bps.description: The H.264 encoder's target bitrate. The encoder opens once at start-up, so a change applies after recordd restarts (restart the edgepilot service or reboot).
param.display.enabled.label: Display power
param.display.enabled.description: Turns only the backlight on or off; the LCD keeps its picture.
param.display.enabled.increase: Turns the backlight PWM back on at the saved brightness.
param.display.enabled.decrease: Sets the backlight PWM duty to 0, so the screen goes fully dark.
param.display.brightness_percent.label: Brightness
param.display.brightness_percent.descrip: Backlight PWM3 (10 kHz) duty. The real duty is brightness × the board maximum (disp_max_backlight in /boot/board). The value is kept while the display is off.
param.display.brightness_percent.decreas: The screen gets dimmer. Use the power switch to turn it off fully.
param.display.alert_volume_percent.label: Alert volume
param.display.alert_volume_percent.descr: Volume of the alerts on the board speaker (engage, disengage, refused engage, take control, unavailable, departure). overlayd applies it within 1 s and plays one confirmation tone per change. With EDGEPILOT_ALERT_SOUND=0 or no speaker there is neither sound nor tone.
param.display.camera_offset_m.label: Camera lateral offset
param.display.camera_offset_m.descriptio: When the board sits off the car's centre, shifts the image so the model sees it from the centre (as sunnypilot's camera offset does). It applies in Lane and Laneless modes and moves the HUD lines too. The shift is based on the road plane, so objects above the road (lead cars and the like) look sheared, more so at larger offsets; like sunnypilot it is limited to ±0.35 m. A change moves at 0.1 m/s.
param.display.camera_offset_m.increase: The car moves left within the lane (if the board sits left of the car's centre, enter that distance as +).
param.display.camera_height_m.label: Camera height
param.display.camera_height_m.descriptio: Height of the camera above the road. It sets the size of the lateral offset correction and places the lead in the image for the optical-flow lead track that vision cruise uses. Set it to the real height.
param.display.camera_height_m.increase: The same lateral offset has a smaller effect.
param.display.camera_height_m.decrease: The same lateral offset has a larger effect.
param.display.calibration_use_flow.label: Flow calibration
param.display.calibration_use_flow.descr: Takes the warp's pitch and yaw from the optical-flow estimate (the camera's direction of travel measured in the video). The estimate is used only once usable (3 or more blocks, about 25 s straight above 40 km/h, block standard deviation up to 0.5°); until then the model pose calibration is used. Flow cannot measure roll, so roll stays the pose calibration's. Flow is measured and saved whether this is on or off. It cannot change while engaged, and a change moves the warp over about 6–15 s, depending on the difference. The state and the gap between the two estimates are on the Vehicle tab's camera calibration card.
param.display.calibration_use_flow.incre: The flow estimate drives the warp once usable, removing the yaw drift (−0.2 to −0.5°) that came from the model pose following the warp only in part.
param.display.calibration_use_flow.decre: Only the model pose calibration is used (the earlier behaviour).
